sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 14.7% a year from $96.6 billion in FY2017 to $331.8 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F221].
Operating income grew faster, at 20.5% a year, lifting operating margin from 30.1% to 46.8% [F31][F40][F223][F41][F50].
FY2026 was the sharpest step, with revenue up 17.8% on Microsoft Cloud growth and Azure [D472][P17].
FY2018 broke the pattern, net income falling 35.0% on the TCJA charge, then FY2019 rebounded 136.8% on a $2.6 billion intangible-transfer tax benefit [D48][D101][P61].
Microsoft Cloud reached 64.6% of revenue in FY2026 and contributed 16.2pp of the 17.8% growth [D566][D568][D472].
Server products and cloud services added 11.0pp, with Azure and other cloud services growing 41% on demand across workloads [D642][P12].
Microsoft 365 Commercial products and cloud services added 5.1pp, with cloud revenue up 17% on Copilot and E5 [D649][P14].
Operating leverage was strong: incremental operating margin was 53.3% and operating costs grew 7.4% against 17.8% revenue growth [D498][D491][D472].
Diluted EPS grew 31.6% against 31.3% net income growth, as the diluted share count fell 0.2% [D476][D474][D493].
Operating margin of 46.8% is a window high, 5.1pp above the 41.7% median and 16.7pp above the 30.1% FY2017 low [F50][D974][D975][D973].
Gross margin slipped 0.9pp to 67.9%, below its 68.2% median, as cost of revenue grew 21.1% against 17.8% revenue growth [F30][D486][D981][D489][D472].
Intelligent Cloud gross margin percentage fell on continued AI infrastructure investment and mix shift to Azure, partly offset by Azure efficiency gains [P11].
R&D fell to 10.7% of revenue, a window low, and selling and marketing to 8.0%, so operating margin still rose 1.2pp [D450][D985][D451][D487].
Net margin rose 4.2pp to 40.3%, helped by $6.5 billion of OpenAI-related gains in other income [D488][F70][P7].
Operating cash flow rose 34.4% to $182.9 billion, 55.1% of revenue, on higher customer cash receipts and lower tax payments [D477][F100][D457][P1].
Free cash flow fell 6.5% to $67.0 billion as capex rose 79.6% to $115.9 billion, a 20.2% margin and window low [D478][F120][D479][F110][D456][D982].
Free cash flow covered only 0.50x of net income, against a 0.91x median, and capex ran 3.38x D&A [D460][D990][D461].
The investing outflow of $139.5 billion reflected a $51.4 billion rise in property additions and $22.2 billion for component purchases [F130][P1].
Net cash was $72.9 billion, 22.0% of revenue, in the 83rd percentile of six software peers against a -7.2% median [D465][D466][D1006][D1007].
Total debt fell 6.6% to $40.3 billion while cash and investments rose 2.9% to $113.2 billion [D495][D464][D494][D463].
Buybacks of $22.3 billion plus dividends of $26.4 billion used 72.7% of free cash flow [X147][X157][D468].
The current ratio of 1.23x is a window low against a 1.93x median, as current liabilities grew 13.1% a year [F200][D991][D993][F233].
Free cash flow stayed below 80% of net income for two years, at 0.70x in FY2025 and 0.50x in FY2026, the window low [R1][D406][D460][D988].
The gap is capex-led rather than earnings-quality-led, but it is the clearest break in the cash story and ranks 20th percentile against peers [D1002][D1008].
FY2017 pretax income, tax and receivables were later restated, and the pack keeps first-reported values, so FY2017 ratios are not comparable [R2][R3][R4][X95][X105][X213].
Product revenue members overlap, summing to 180% of FY2026 consolidated revenue, so they should not be added [R5].
If free cash flow margin stays below the 30.3% median or capex exceeds 34.9% of revenue, the cash-conversion trend is confirmed rather than reversed [D984][D455].
If operating margin holds above the 41.7% median despite AI infrastructure spend, the margin expansion is durable [D975].
If Microsoft Cloud growth falls below its 26.9% FY2026 rate, the largest growth driver is decelerating [D567].
